concepts.quote: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;

concepts.label: Infant Head Support
concepts.definition: Permitted discreet support of an infant's head in a photograph.
concepts.quote: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.

scope_quotes: d. Infants pose a particular challenge. The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained:

concepts.label: Infant Head Tilt

concepts.label: Parent Face Prohibition
concepts.definition: Prohibition against a parent's face appearing in an infant's photograph.
concepts.quote: A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

scope_quotes: in the photograph of the infant
summary: A parent's face must not appear in the photograph of the infant.
quote: A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

concepts.label: Photograph Timeliness and Likeness
concepts.definition: Recommendation regarding photograph recency (six months), likeness, and applicant identification.
concepts.quote: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).

concepts.quote: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant;

concepts.label: Passport Photograph Reuse
concepts.definition: Descriptive possibility of applicants wishing to reuse photographs from naturalization or citizenship certificates.
concepts.quote: Applicants may wish to re-use a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization.

concepts.label: Certificate Photo Recency Warning
concepts.definition: Cautionary note that certificate photographs might not satisfy the six-month timeliness standard despite recent issuance.
concepts.quote: Be aware that even if the certificate itself was recently issued, because of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services processing times, the photograph may not have been taken within six months of submitting the application.
